title: Navigating comics: an empirical and theoretical approach to strategies of reading comic page layouts
key_findings: 145 participants numbered empty panels on 12 layouts; Z-path used ~94% in a canonical grid
Blockage: 91/145 read the left vertical stack first instead of the Z-path
Separation Z-path ~0.72; staggering ~0.90 (trend only); inset: outer dominant panel first 60%
Upper-left panel almost always starts the page (0.96); left-to-right preferred 93 vs 21
Proposes Assemblage (grouped areas, smooth paths, no jumping, no gaps) and ordered preference rules
Frequent comic readers used blockage paths more; frequent manga readers used L->R entry less
practical_applications: Use plain grids for broad audiences
Avoid or cue blockage layouts
Start the page with a clear top-left panel
limitations: Self-selected Comic-Con sample (2004)
Empty panels, no content
Self-reported expertise

title: Navigating comics II: constraints on the reading order of comic page layouts
key_findings: All departures from a grid (blockage/staggering, separation, overlap) pushed readers off the Z-path
Deviation was graded: the lower the rightward gutter, the less the Z-path; at full blockage Z-path <10%
Wider gutters increased group-by-group reading
Notes written Japanese can run right-to-left in vertical columns, unlike L->R English
practical_applications: Keep gutters contiguous when you want rows to read as rows
Use gutter width deliberately to group panels
limitations: Empty-panel task
Author preprint read; published in Applied Cognitive Psychology 29:193-199

title: The architecture of visual narrative comprehension: the interaction of narrative structure and page layout in understanding comics
key_findings: Z-path in grid 95%, staggered 89%, separated 71%, blockage 31% (synthesis)
Narrative constituents and layout tiers are not isomorphic; they operate in parallel
Suggests (untested) Initials at page ends drive page turns and splash pages act as Peaks
practical_applications: Align scene changes and cliffhangers with page/slide boundaries as a hypothesis to test
limitations: Focused review of the author's own work
Layout-narrative mappings are observations, not tested

title: Framing attention in Japanese and American comics: cross-cultural differences in attentional structure
authors: Neil Cohn, Amaro Taylor-Weiner, Suzanne Grossman
key_findings: 30 books (US mainstream, US indy, Japanese manga), ~300 panels each, coded Macro/Mono/Micro/Amorphic
US comics: Macro ~ Mono, few Micro/Amorphic; manga: Mono dominant, more Micro and Amorphic
Shot types track genre more than country
Interpreted as manga using panels as a spotlight of attention; convention is an alternative explanation
practical_applications: Vary attentional framing: Amorphic for mood pauses, Micro for product/detail inserts
limitations: 10 books per group; translated shonen only
Moderate shot-coding reliability (kappa 0.54)
Cognition link inferred

title: Your brain on comics: a cognitive model of visual narrative comprehension
key_findings: PINS model: semantics (mental model, updating) and narrative structure (categories, constituents) processed in parallel
Categories: Establisher, Initial, (Prolongation), Peak, Release; plus conjunction and Refiner (head-modifier) schemas
People delete Establishers/Releases more than Peaks/Initials; missing core panels are detected more accurately
N400 indexes semantic access; anterior negativity narrative structure; P600 updating/inference
Visual language fluency (VLFI) modulates ERPs, reaction and viewing times; manga readership changes processing of Environmental-Conjunction
practical_applications: Plan each panel's narrative role; cut peripheral panels first
Keep inference load low for non-comic audiences
limitations: Model synthesises mostly one lab's work
Mostly wordless Western strips
license: CC BY (open access, Topics in Cognitive Science)

title: Zooming in on visual narrative comprehension
key_findings: Panels zoomed to the regions fixated by earlier readers (about 13% of the panel area) were rated easier to understand than non-fixated or incongruous controls (7-point scale: 4.2 vs 1.8; full panels 6.1) and were viewed more similarly to the originals.
Non-fixated or incongruous crops were harder
Fixation-based inset panels also highlighted key content; modifications affected subsequent panels
practical_applications: Crop tightly to the informative region; use inserts/Refiners for product details
limitations: Self-paced lab task, six-panel strips
Memory & Cognition 49:451-466
Spot-check C1 2026-11-25: corrected.

title: Reading without words: eye movements in the comprehension of comic strips
authors: Tom Foulsham, Dean Wybrow, Neil Cohn
key_findings: Panels in original order were understood faster with fewer fixations than in random order
Random order produced more regressions
Narrative context changed where people looked inside panels
practical_applications: Coherent order lowers effort; scrambled or unclear order costs attention
limitations: Wordless Peanuts strips
Lab eye tracking

title: Being explicit about the implicit: inference generating techniques in visual narrative
key_findings: Speech balloons and motion lines are bound morphemes (affixes) that attach to stems; framing out the stem triggers inference
Peak Drop: deliberate omission of the Peak, inferred from Initial + Release
Suppletive panels (action stars, fight clouds, poof clouds) and text substitution (a sound effect replaces the Peak)
practical_applications: Use Peak Drop for before/after and gentle handling of sad or violent beats
SFX can stand in for an action
limitations: Theoretical/descriptive, corpus examples; not exhaustive

title: (Pea)nuts and bolts of visual narrative: structure and meaning in sequential image comprehension
authors: Neil Cohn, Martin Paczynski, Ray Jackendoff, Phillip J. Holcomb, Gina R. Kuperberg
key_findings: Compared Normal, Semantic-only, Structural-only and Scrambled strips
Reaction times fastest for Normal, slowest for Scrambled, intermediate for the others
N300/N400 smallest for Normal sequences: structure + meaning together ease processing
practical_applications: Both a coherent narrative arc and related content are needed
limitations: Only abstract read in detail; DOI and Cognitive Psychology 65 (2012) 1-38 confirmed from the PDF header

title: The limits of time and transitions: challenges to theories of sequential image comprehension
key_findings: Critiques McCloud's six transitions as linear panel-to-panel relations without hierarchy
Argues closure is an additive inference made at the next panel, not in the gutter
Critiques Groensteen's arthrology as making no testable predictions; proposes hierarchic grouping (grammar)
practical_applications: Treat McCloud transitions as a planning vocabulary, not a cognitive model
limitations: Theoretical argument; Studies in Comics 1(1)

title: Beyond speech balloons and thought bubbles: the integration of text and image
key_findings: Four text-image interfaces: Inherent, Emergent (balloons/tails), Adjoined (captions near), Independent
Integration tempered by Gestalt grouping and semantic features
Balloon carriers link text content to a root (speaker)
practical_applications: Balloon-free captions are Adjoined: speaker must be signalled by position, colour or font
limitations: Theoretical, Semiotica 197

title: The vocabulary of manga: visual morphology in dialects of Japanese Visual Language
key_findings: Described and categorised 73 conventional graphic schemas in manga (e.g. nosebleeds, sleep bubbles)
Corpus of 20 books: most schemas recur in shonen and shojo, at different proportions ('dialects')
practical_applications: Use recognised symbols to carry emotion for faceless characters
limitations: Only abstract read in this session

title: Pow, punch, pika, and chu: the structure of sound effects in genres of American comics and Japanese manga
authors: Nimish K. Pratha, Natalie Avunjian, Neil Cohn
key_findings: US mainstream comics used 100% onomatopoetic SFX, indy comics also some descriptive SFX (Punch!)
Shojo manga used more gitaigo (state-mimicking) and hiragana; shonen more giongo and katakana
In English a similar function is carried by font stylisation
practical_applications: Choose SFX type (sound vs state word) and lettering style by genre and tone
limitations: Small genre corpora; Multimodal Communication 5(2)

title: Navigating meaning in the spatial layouts of comics: a cross-cultural corpus analysis
authors: Irmak Hacimusaoglu, Bien Klomberg, Neil Cohn
key_findings: Corpus of 134 annotated comics (North America, Europe, Asia)
Within-row transitions change the situation least; across rows and pages more
Page boundaries align with spatial-location changes; Asian comics less constrained by layout
practical_applications: Put scene/location changes on page or slide boundaries
limitations: Only abstract read (publisher blocked); correlational

title: Navigating the narrative: an eye-tracking study of readers' strategies when reading comic page layouts
authors: Clare Kirtley, Chris Murray, Phillip B. Vaughan, Benjamin W. Tatler
key_findings: Eye tracking replicated the dominant influence of panel external structure on navigation
Text location inside panels affected order in ambiguous layouts
practical_applications: Use balloon position to cue reading order when a layout is irregular
limitations: Only abstract read (publisher blocked)

title: Reading comics: the effect of expertise on eye movements
key_findings: 14 experts vs 17 non-experts; experts made more and larger saccades
Experts attended more to images; non-experts needed more and longer fixations on text
practical_applications: For general audiences keep text short; images should carry the story
limitations: Small sample; GLMM with layout/text controls
license: CC BY (Journal of Eye Movement Research)

title: Picturing words: the semantics of speech balloons
key_findings: Speech and thought bubbles analysed as quotational event modification in a dynamic picture semantics
Balloons are symbolic elements inside iconic pictures; non-verbal affixes (motion lines, lightbulbs) can be analysed similarly
practical_applications: Balloon content is read as a quotation attached to the depicted speaker/event
limitations: Formal semantics proceedings paper (Amsterdam Colloquium); no empirical data

title: The secret art of comedy manga: analisis struktur kishotenketsu pada komik populer Jepang
authors: Ni Kadek Karisma Dewi, Ni Nyoman Puspa Dewi, Luh Putu Leoni Pramesti, I Nyoman Larry Julianto
key_findings: Yonkoma structure: Ki = intro (panel 1), Sho = development (2), Ten = unexpected twist/climax (3), Ketsu = conclusion that makes the reader rethink the twist (4)
Qualitative analysis of Gekkan Shojo Nozaki-kun ch.101: structure gives a clear, consistent message and scales to longer plots
practical_applications: Use ki-sho-ten-ketsu for 4-slide gentle gags and reflective stories
limitations: Descriptive qualitative study of one manga; Indonesian design journal

title: Review of 'The Art of Thai Comics: A Century of Strips and Stripes' by Nicolas Verstappen
key_findings: Thai comics peaked 1980s-2000s; first Siamese comic strip late 1920s (Pong Gab Priaw)
Temple-mural tradition: panels with minimal captions and detailed backgrounds, colour with narrative codes
Manga has dominated Thai comics since the 1980s; Thai comics characterised by eclectic mixing (lai rot)
practical_applications: Detailed, meaningful backgrounds and folk-tale retelling fit Thai visual heritage
limitations: Book review, not primary research; Journal of the Siam Society 110(1)

title: The symbolization of sounds in Thai onomatopoeic words
key_findings: Data from Thai dictionaries and 40 Japanese-to-Thai translated comics
Most Thai sound-symbolic words are monomorphemic or reduplicated
Meanings relate to human behaviours, activities and surroundings
practical_applications: Thai SFX design: use single syllables and reduplication
limitations: Only the abstract page read; full PDF blocked by a bot check

title: Memes in a digital world: reconciling with a conceptual troublemaker
key_findings: Internet memes = groups of related items circulated, imitated and transformed by many users
Three dimensions: content, form, stance (participation, keying, communicative function)
Spread through mimicry and remix; form is copied most faithfully while content/stance shift
practical_applications: Design comic templates with fixed form and swappable content; match stance to brand
limitations: Two qualitative case studies; 2013 platforms

title: Understanding Comics: The Invisible Art
key_findings: Closure and six panel transitions (moment, action, subject, scene, aspect, non-sequitur) as described in Cohn2010TimeTransitions
practical_applications: Vocabulary for planning transitions
limitations: Book not read this session; content known via Cohn2010TimeTransitions and a 1998 IEEE review record (the URL/DOI is that 1998 review, not the book)

title: Comics and Sequential Art: Principles and Practices from the Legendary Cartoonist
key_findings: Existence of 1985/1990 and 2008 editions confirmed via OpenAlex records
practical_applications: Classic practitioner textbook on sequential art
limitations: Not read this session; no findings claimed

title: The System of Comics (trans. Bart Beaty, Nick Nguyen)
key_findings: Per search summaries: spatio-topia (space + place of panels), arthrology (relations among images), restricted vs general arthrology, braiding (tressage)
practical_applications: Motif repetition across distant panels/episodes
limitations: Only search summaries read; French original 1999, English 2007 (University Press of Mississippi)

title: Sticker guidelines (static) - LINE Creators Market
key_findings: Sets of 8/16/24/32/40; sticker max 370x320 px, <=1 MB; main 240x240; tab 96x74; PNG transparent; >=72 dpi RGB; even dimensions; ~10 px margin; ZIP <=60 MB
Recommended: everyday expressions/messages; not recommended: objects/scenery, overly long images, low variety
Prohibited: advertising, requests for personal info, sexual/violent content, under-age drinking/smoking
practical_applications: Spec sheet for sticker sets
limitations: Platform rules change; re-check before submission

title: Animated sticker guidelines - LINE Creators Market
key_findings: Sets of 8/16/24; max 320x270 px (one side >=270); 5-20 frames; <=4 s; 1-4 loops; APNG with .png; <=1 MB each; main 240x240; tab 96x74
practical_applications: Spec sheet for animated stickers
limitations: Platform rules change

title: Creator's Resource Handbook and Before You Publish Checklist (WEBTOON CANVAS)
key_findings: Vertical format: reader sees one panel at a time; max 2 panels on screen; <=3 balloons/panel; 1-2 sentences per balloon; diamond stacking
Min 200 px between panels in a scene; 600-1000 px for location/scene transition; vary panel size; impact panels
Images <800 px wide and <1280 px tall, <=2 MB each, <=20 MB / 100 images; JPG/PNG
Thumbnails 1080x1080 (<500 KB) and 1080x1920 (<700 KB), no text; launch with 3 episodes; font 12-30 px typical
practical_applications: Pacing and spec rules for webtoon and scroll-pan clips
limitations: Editorial guidance from the platform, not reader research; year not printed

title: Tips for Creating Vertical Scrolling Webtoons
key_findings: Canvas 800 px wide per WEBTOON spec; export in sections <=1280 px
Spacing gives readers rest and time for text; larger gaps mark scene change
Gradient maps (e.g. sepia) for flashback; colour can extend beyond panels; dialogue before character suggests thought
practical_applications: Practical webtoon production tips
limitations: Practitioner tutorial; no pixel values for spacing

title: Comic Book Grammar & Tradition
key_findings: Tails point to the mouth and end ~50-60% of the way to the head; joined balloons = one train of thought
Off-panel: tail to border or none; thought balloons largely replaced by captions
Burst = shout; dashed = whisper; lightning tail = radio; caption types: location/time, internal, spoken, editorial; avoid tangents
Bold italic for emphasis; double dashes for interruption; ellipses for trailing
practical_applications: Lettering conventions for balloons and captions (adapt for Thai: no caps)
limitations: US English conventions; craft, not research

title: Instagram Now Allows Up to 20 Photos and Videos for Carousel Posts
key_findings: Instagram raised the carousel limit from 10 to 20 photos/videos, rolling out worldwide on 8 Aug 2024
practical_applications: Carousel comics can run up to 20 slides
limitations: News report, not Instagram's Help Center; aspect-ratio rules not covered
